what_the_research_says: Manganese ore in this belt occurs specifically within the Mansar Formation of the Sausar Group, at three recognised horizons near the bottom, middle and top of the formation, giving rise to the major deposits including Ukwa, Bharweli, Ramrama, Tirodi and Sukli-Sitapatore.
source_title: Hierarchy Amongst Rocks of Sausar Group - Evidences from Seoni-Balaghat Area, Madhya Pradesh, India

what_the_research_says: The Sausar Group succession is, in ascending order: Sitasaongi Formation, Lohangi Formation, Mansar Formation (manganese-bearing), Chorbaoli Formation, Junewani Formation, and Bichua Formation, with the Tirodi (biotite) Gneiss generally treated as the older basement complex.
source_title: Structural Evolution of Sausar Group around Parseoni, Nagpur District, Maharashtra: Its Implication for Stratigraphy
author_or_organization: Journal of the Geological Society of India (ResearchGate)

what_the_research_says: Independent regional stratigraphic compilations (Straczek et al. 1956; Narayanaswami et al. 1963; Basu 1958) all place two manganese-ore-bearing horizons within/adjacent to a 'Manganese Group' of muscovite schist with gondite, bracketed by the Chorbaoli/Junewani and Lohangi-equivalent formations, over an Amgaon Gneissic Complex basement in the south.
source_title: Regional Exploration Proposal for Manganese Ore (Lanjera-Futala Block)
author_or_organization: National Mineral Exploration Trust (NMET), Government of India

factor_or_relationship: Structural control of ore emplacement (shear zones / mylonites)
what_the_research_says: Field relations - shear-zone association of every mapped manganese deposit, S-C fabric in the ore, pinch-and-swell ore geometry, and cross-cutting (non-co-planar) contacts with host-rock foliation at Tirodi, Bharweli and Ukwa - are cited as evidence that ore bodies were emplaced along shear/mylonite zones parallel to the regional S1 schistosity, rather than being purely of sedimentary origin.
source_title: Evidences Towards Hydrothermal Origin of Manganese Deposits of Sukli-Sitapathore-Tirodi-Ramrama-Bharweli-Ukwa Belt of Madhya Pradesh, India

what_the_research_says: Ore bands are folded along later (S2/S3) axial trends producing a sinuous outcrop pattern, and ore-band terminations at Kandri and Mansar mines are attributed to fold-interference effects, indicating that polyphase folding directly controls ore-body shape and continuity.
source_title: Structural Evolution of Sausar Group around Parseoni, Nagpur District, Maharashtra: Its Implication for Stratigraphy
author_or_organization: Journal of the Geological Society of India (ResearchGate)

factor_or_relationship: Polyphase deformation / multiple lineament trend sets
what_the_research_says: Detailed structural analysis at Chikla-Sitekesa (Bhandara district) recognises four generations of foliation (S1-S4) and six generations of lineation (L1-L6), reflecting a triclinic, multi-phase deformation history with several distinct structural trend sets rather than a single fault/lineament orientation.
source_title: Structural Analysis of a Part of the Sausar Group Rocks in Chikla-Sitekesa Area, Bhandara District, Maharashtra
author_or_organization: Journal of the Geological Society of India

factor_or_relationship: Tirodi Gneiss as basement / contact metamorphism
what_the_research_says: The Tirodi biotite gneiss is treated by several workers as basement to the Sausar Group across a disconformable/unconformable contact, and is cited as the heat source for zoned contact-metamorphic aureoles developed in adjacent Bichua Formation metacarbonates in western Balaghat.
source_title: Contact Metamorphism of Calcareous Metasediments of Sausars from Western Balaghat Area of Madhya Pradesh, India and Its Implication in Sausar Stratigraphy

what_the_research_says: Manganese-rich rocks in the belt carry a metamorphic mineral assemblage (rhodochrosite, pyroxmangite, magnetite, garnet, Mn-cummingtonite, pyrophanite, quartz +/- tephroite) interpreted to have formed at roughly 500-550 degrees C, i.e. lower-to-mid amphibolite facies conditions.
source_title: Structural Evolution of Sausar Group around Parseoni, Nagpur District, Maharashtra: Its Implication for Stratigraphy
author_or_organization: Journal of the Geological Society of India (ResearchGate)

what_the_research_says: Gondite (Mn-silicate rock dominated by spessartine, rhodonite, quartz, Mn-diopside and related phases) is interbanded with the manganese oxide ore and is described as an important stratigraphic marker of the Mansar Formation horizon; a related gondite occurrence is also documented at Gowari Wadhona on the belt's westernmost flank, i.e. outside the main ore-horizon trend.
source_title: Mineralogy and genesis of the metamorphosed manganese silicate rocks (gondite) of Gowari Wadhona, Madhya Pradesh, India

factor_or_relationship: Ore mineral assemblage variation between mines
what_the_research_says: X-ray diffraction and ore petrography show that manganese ore mineral assemblages differ significantly between the Bharweli, Tirodi and Ukwa mines, indicating some variation in metamorphic/genetic history along the belt even though all three lie within the same regional ore horizon system.
source_title: Manganese Ore Minerals Assemblages and Mineral Paragenesis with the Help of Ore Petrography and XRD Studies of Balaghat District, (M.P.) India

factor_or_relationship: Structural control at Chikla Mine (synform/fold-core hosting)
what_the_research_says: At Chikla Mine, the manganese ore occurs at the contact of Mansar Formation mica schist with Sitasaongi Formation quartz-mica schist, and the ore body itself is described as occupying the core of a plunging synform, with mining following the synform's axial trace through several parallel, tightly folded ore bands.
source_title: Chikla mines, Chikala, Bhandara District, Nagpur Division, Maharashtra, India (locality record)
author_or_organization: Mindat.org (Hudson Institute of Mineralogy, citing Mitra 1965; Sarkar et al. 1977)

factor_or_relationship: MOIL mine locations and operating status
what_the_research_says: MOIL operates underground and opencast manganese mines in Balaghat district (Madhya Pradesh) and in Nagpur/Bhandara districts (Maharashtra); the Dongri Buzurg mine (Bhandara district) is specifically an opencast mine producing manganese-dioxide-grade ore.
source_title: About MOIL

what_the_research_says: As of the reporting period, MOIL operated ten mines in total: seven underground (Kandri, Munsar, Beldongri, Gumgaon, Chikla, Balaghat, Ukwa) and three opencast (Dongri Buzurg, Sitapatore, Tirodi), with the Balaghat mine described as the deepest underground manganese mine in Asia.
source_title: Candid conversation with CMD MOIL

what_the_research_says: Sentinel-2's MSI instrument carries several bands spanning the ~0.9 micron ferric-iron absorption feature (where older sensors such as ASTER/Landsat had only one band), giving it genuine, literature-documented utility for surface iron-oxide and lithological/alteration mapping at regional-to-continental scale.
source_title: Using Sentinel-2 MSI for mapping iron oxide minerals on a continental and global scale
author_or_organization: NASA Astrophysics Data System (AGU Fall Meeting abstract)

factor_or_relationship: Sentinel-2 band-ratio indices for iron-oxide / alteration
what_the_research_says: Diagnostic multispectral band ratios such as B4/B3, B4/B2, B11/B12 and B12/B8A are reported in the remote-sensing literature as proxies for ferric-oxide and hydroxyl/clay alteration minerals, and have been applied together with lineament analysis to delineate structurally controlled mineral prospecting corridors elsewhere in the world.
source_title: Mapping of mineral resources and lithological units: a review of remote sensing techniques

what_the_research_says: Comparative studies find that Sentinel-2 offers higher spatial resolution but comparatively limited SWIR bands, while ASTER's additional SWIR bands and Landsat's broader spectral/thermal coverage each contribute complementary lithological/alteration information, motivating multi-sensor data fusion for mineral mapping.
source_title: Multi-Sensor Remote Sensing for Hydrothermal Alteration Mapping and Copper Prospectivity in the Skardu Region, Pakistan (context article/figure)

factor_or_relationship: Remote sensing + geophysics integration for Mn (and associated metal) mineralisation elsewhere
what_the_research_says: In an analogous Precambrian metallogenic belt (Anti-Atlas, Morocco), Sentinel-2 spectral anomalies were found to spatially correlate with mapped faults/shear zones and with Cu-Mn-Co-Ba-Fe mineralisation, supporting the general concept that structurally controlled multi-element mineralisation produces co-located spectral and geophysical/structural anomalies.
source_title: Remote sensing and aeromagnetic data integration for mapping Cu, Mn, Co, Ba, and Fe Mineralization: A Case study from Ait Semgane, Anti-Atlas, Morocco

what_the_research_says: Dense sulphide/oxide ore bodies commonly produce local positive gravity anomalies relative to their host rock, and horizontal-gradient-magnitude processing of potential-field data is a standard technique for locating geological contacts and faults; this is a general mineral-exploration-geophysics principle used here as a scientifically reasonable proxy, since no Sausar-belt-specific gravity survey publication was located during this research pass.
source_title: (general mineral-exploration geophysics principle - no single Sausar-belt-specific source located)

factor_or_relationship: Weathering / laterite development in central Indian uplands
what_the_research_says: Lateritic weathering profiles are a well-documented, widespread near-surface phenomenon across central Indian Precambrian terrains and can locally enrich surface iron/manganese oxides independent of primary ore genesis; this is used here as a scientifically reasonable confounding factor rather than a Sausar-belt-specific measurement.
source_title: (general central-Indian regolith/weathering literature - no single Sausar-belt-specific source located)

what_the_research_says: Quartzite and gneissic units are relatively resistant to weathering and typically form ridges, while marble/calc-silicate and schistose units are less resistant and typically form valleys - a standard structural-geomorphology relationship applied here as a general principle rather than a site-specific DEM measurement for this belt.
source_title: (general structural-geomorphology principle - no single Sausar-belt-specific source located)
